objective: Compare what Claude Code's built-in git instructions give the model (commit and PR workflow guidance, safety rules, git status snapshot) with what HolyAgent's own version-control instructions give the root and specialists, and list concrete gaps HolyAgent should cover now that setup turns the built-in ones off.
scope: HolyAgent's VCS text: packages/integrations/claude/src (root and specialist section files, hooks that add VCS context), docs/commit-authorship.md, docs/hooks.md, the holyagent vcs commit/pr implementation in packages/runtime.

Claude Code's built-in git guidance: what includeGitInstructions removes (from Claude Code docs or the plugin's own notes; if the exact text is not available locally, say so and work from documented behavior).
constraints: Read-only. For each gap give the rule Claude Code had, whether HolyAgent covers it (path:line), and a one-sentence proposed instruction for HolyAgent. Mark gaps that matter for safety (e.g. never skip hooks, never amend others' commits, never commit secrets, check status/diff before commit) separately from nice-to-haves.
Keep working until done; stop and report. Report in under 500 words.

result: HolyAgent covers the identity, force-push, protected-branch, staging-scope and PR-text rules. It has no coverage of eight rules that guard against unsafe or lossy git actions, and it provides no git state snapshot.

Caveat: the built-in text is not available locally. The only local facts are `/home/user/holyagent/.claude/settings.json:4` (`includeGitInstructions: false`) and `/home/user/holyagent/docs/usage.md:64` (it removes the commit and PR instructions and the status snapshot). The built-in rules below come from documented and remembered behavior, so treat them as unverified.

**Covered, for reference**
- Identity: refuses an agent's identity (`packages/runtime/src/vcs/commit.ts:45-52`).
- Force-push and protected branches: `root/identity.md:9` and `root/version-control.md:11`, plus a one-line `vcs-reminder` hook (`packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts:156-158`).
- Staging exactly the named paths: refuses staged-outside-scope and nothing-to-commit (`commit.ts:269-283`). It also removes the need for the built-in "add specific files, not `-A`" rule.
- Repository hooks run on `vcs commit` (`commit.ts:253`).
- Attribution and commit/PR text: `root/version-control.md:5`, `requirements/commit-text.md`, `root/pr-text.md`.
- Specialists make no git writes: `specialist/state-changes.md:3`.

**Safety gaps**

| # | Built-in rule | HolyAgent coverage | Proposed instruction |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Never skip hooks (`--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`) | Absent from the instruction text. `commit.ts` passes no skip flag, but raw `git commit` is unblocked and the hook (`hook.ts:158`) never mentions it. | "Never bypass hooks or signing (`--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, `-c commit.gpgsign=false`) unless the user asks." |
| S2 | If a pre-commit hook fails, fix the issue and make a NEW commit; never `--amend` | Absent. The `commit.ts` docs say only that hooks run. | "When a hook fails the commit did not happen: fix it, re-stage and run `vcs commit` again; never amend." |
| S3 | Do not amend commits you did not just create, or published ones | Partial: `version-control.md:11` says a rewrite of published history goes to the user. Nothing on amend or rebase. | "Amend only your own unpushed commit and only when asked; never `rebase -i`, `reset --hard` or `commit --amend` on published or others' commits." |
| S4 | Never commit secrets (`.env`, credentials); warn if the user asks | Absent. `AGENTS.md`/`docs/commit-authorship.md` do not cover it. | "Before `vcs commit`, check the paths for secrets (`.env`, keys, tokens) and refuse or ask." |
| S5 | Check `git status` and `git diff` before committing, and `git log` for style | Partial: `version-control.md:7` points to repository conventions and history. Nothing requires a diff check. | "Read `git status` and `git diff` for the paths before `vcs commit`, so the commit matches the Assignment." |
| S6 | Never update git config | Absent. Nothing stops the root from changing `user.name` to get past the identity check. | "Never edit git config; if the identity is refused, report it." |
| S7 | Never run interactive git (`-i`) | Absent. | "Run git non-interactively; never use `-i` or open an editor." |
| S8 | Only commit when asked | Absent. The root commits as part of the workflow; this is a policy choice. | "Commit and push only as the Intent's order or the user requires." |

**Nice-to-haves**
- N1: Git status snapshot (branch, default branch, short status, recent commits). Absent: `session-reminder.md` has none, and no `SessionStart` hook adds git state. Proposal: "Run `git status -sb` and `git log -5 --oneline` at the first commit step."
- N2: PR workflow (check the branch tracks a remote, diff against the base across all commits, push, then return the URL). It is partial: `version-control.md:11` covers push, `pr.ts:114-153` posts through REST and records the PR, and `pr-text.md` covers the text. There is no instruction to read all commits since the base. Proposal: "Write PR text from `git diff <base>...HEAD` and the full commit list, and report the URL."
- N3: Check for a PR template. Absent. Proposal: "Use the repository's PR template when one exists."
- N4: Avoid empty commits. Handled in code by `NothingToCommit` (`commit.ts:283`), so no text is needed.
- N5: Use `gh` for GitHub URLs. Absent. Proposal: "Read GitHub URLs with `gh`, not a web fetch."

**Coverage hole**
- Every VCS rule is instruction text. `docs/hooks.md:88` confirms nothing blocks a raw git write, and the only hook adds one line and only when the command matches `git ... commit|push` (`hook.ts:166`).
- S1 to S3 are therefore reachable through raw git, for example `git commit --no-verify` or `git reset --hard`.
- The `vcs-reminder` text could be extended to cover S1 to S3.
